ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of SGD 4.02 to the rider for the ~2.85 km unmetered detour distance (RD-2/RD-1) and remind the driver that RD-1 requires the shortest and most direct route absent any reasonable cause or prior agreement with the rider.

segment_findings.reason: Orchard Blvd / Delfi Orchard southbound branch (≈1.2819,103.8508 → 1.2781,103.8583), followed south-west while the quoted route proceeds north-east toward Tanglin/Kim Seng; offset 0.4–1.3 km, ~1.3–1.4 km extra, far above the 0.2 km noise tolerance. No rider consent in chat and no traffic incident (RD-4(a) absent; band-3 records are on the quoted route and band records alone never exempt, RD-4(b)); RD-3 gives no exemption as this was a driver-chosen routing, not a rider-named stop. Un-exempted → counts under RD-1/RD-2.

Fort Canning / Singapore River loop (≈1.2797,103.8594 → 1.2939,103.8639, ~5.5–7 min), running parallel to but north of the quoted CTE alignment before rejoining at 1.2943,103.8655. Offset ≈0.6–0.8 km, ≈1.4–1.5 km extra. No incident on the replaced CTE stretch (traffic.incidents empty) and no rider agreement in the chat before the detour began (RD-5); the driver's 'GPS rerouted me' claim is not rider consent (G11). Un-exempted → counts under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver claims 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me.' The GPS trace contradicts this — it deviates from the quoted alignment by up to ~1.3 km over ~5.5–7 min — and a reroute, even if genuine, is not a rider consent (RD-5; verbal-agreement claims in a statement are not consent, G11). No traffic incident exists to make the deviation a 'reasonable cause' (RD-4).

The rider's assertion that he was never asked is consistent with the chat record (only pickup-arrangement messages, no route discussion), so it is accepted on the route-deviation point; only the remedy is scaled to the reconstructable off-route distance rather than the full 25 km figure in the complaint.
